## Reading the page in the browser

`SHOP_JS` is a script that the module injects into the store page. It
finds these items:

- product cards, add-to-cart buttons, and quantity controls
- the cart count, subtotal, and cart lines
- form fields
- blockers such as cookie banners

The script reads links, text, and common markup from the page. It has no
rules for one store. Page navigation removes the script. The Python code
injects it again when needed.

## Site hints

`SITES` stores facts that the page does not show. These facts include
search and cart URLs for some stores. They also include notes such as
“pick a store first”.
[`site_hint`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/shop.html#site_hint)
returns the entry for a URL host, or `{}` for an unlisted store.
Unlisted stores also work. The module searches them through the store’s
search box.

## Reading the store

These methods are added to fastcdp’s `Page`. Each method returns plain
data.

`shop_prep` injects `SHOP_JS` when the page has no copy of it. It
returns the store platform: `shopify`, `woocommerce`, `bigcommerce`,
`magento`, `next`, or `generic`.

[`shop_products`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_products)
lists the products on the page. Each product has a number in `i`. Use
that number or the title to choose a product. On a product page, the
main product comes first. The other products have the `related` mark.

[`shop_cart`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_cart)
reads the cart item count and subtotal. It uses Shopify’s `/cart.js`
when available. It reads the page for other stores. The `source` key
identifies the source. `shop_lines` reads the cart lines from the cart
page.

`shop_blockers` names blockers such as `cookie-banner`,
`location-required`, `login-required`, `captcha`, and `modal-open`.
[`shop_dismiss`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_dismiss)
clicks cookie banners and closable pop-ups.

A request that cannot run raises
[`ShopError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/shop.html#shoperror).
For example, a product number that is not on the page raises this error.
The error lists the available choices.

## Actions that check their result

[`shop_add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_add)
adds a product selected by number or title. It returns `ok`, `how`, the
product, and the cart `before` and `after` readings.

<table>

<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>ok</code></th>
<th>Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>True</td>
<td>A cart signal changed. A cart signal is the item count, subtotal,
cart lines, or a new confirmation message. <code>how</code> names the
signal as <code>count</code>, <code>subtotal</code>, <code>lines</code>,
or the confirmation message.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>False</td>
<td>Nothing changed. <code>error</code> gives the reason.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>None</td>
<td>The page has no cart count or subtotal to compare. The add is not
confirmed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A title must match a product title exactly or occur within a product
title. An exact match takes priority. A Shopify product can have
variants such as sizes. When several variants are in stock and you pass
no `variant`,
[`shop_add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_add)
returns `need='variant'` and the in-stock variants. It does not choose a
variant. A product with one in-stock variant uses that variant.

`shop_cart_page` opens the cart page and returns the cart with its
lines. `shop_qty` sets the quantity of a line. `shop_remove` removes a
line. Both methods check the cart as
[`shop_add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_add)
does.

## Checkout forms

[`shop_fields`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_fields)
lists every visible form field on the page. Each entry has the field
number `i`, the label, the `autocomplete` token and the current value. A
drop-down entry also lists its options.
[`shop_fields`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_fields)
never returns password values.

[`shop_fill`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_fill)
fills a form from a profile dictionary. The standard keys are
`first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `phone`, `address1`, `address2`,
`city`, `state`, `postcode`, `country`, `company`, `notes` and the
`card_*` keys.
[`match_fields`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/shop.html#match_fields)
decides which field each key goes into. It checks the field’s
`autocomplete` token first, then its name or id, then its label. It uses
the words in `FIELD_MAP`, which include Australian wording such as
“suburb” and “postcode”. Each field is used for one key at most.

A numeric key, such as `'7'`, fills field number 7 from
[`shop_fields`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_fields).
Use it for choices that have no standard key, such as size or delivery
time.

After the fill,
[`shop_fill`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_fill)
reads the form again and reports whether each field holds the value.
`shop_set` sets one field by its number.

`shop_fill(submit=...)` clicks a button or link by its name after the
fill. A name that matches `PAY_RX`, such as “Pay now” or “Place order”,
needs `confirm=True`. Without it,
[`shop_fill`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/mcp.html#shop_fill)
raises
[`ShopError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/shop.html#shoperror)
and fills nothing.

## [`Shop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/shop.html#shop)

The methods above are asynchronous and require a `Page`.
[`Shop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/shop.html#shop) wraps
them as synchronous methods with shorter names: `platform`, `products`,
`cart`, `cart_page`, `lines`, `add`, `set_qty`, `remove`, `fields`,
`set`, `fill`, `blockers`, `dismiss`, `snapshot`, and `md`. The return
type depends on the method. `platform`, `snapshot`, and `md` return
strings. The other listed methods return dictionaries or lists.

[`Shop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/shop.html#shop) also has
`goto`, `open`, `find`, and
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search).
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) tries
the store search URL, the Shopify search page, and the page search box
in that order.

`shop(url)` opens a session. It connects to the debug Chrome and starts
it when needed. It reuses a tab that an earlier
[`shop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#shop) call left
open on the same store. With `resume=True`, it keeps that tab on its
current page instead of going to `url`. The `fossick shop --add 0`
command uses this tab to act on results left by a previous `--search`
command.

## Tests

The offline tests cover site hints, profile key matching, cart change
detection, product selection by number or title, the payment button
guard, and cart line lookup. The cells under Live stores need the debug
Chrome and network access. The tests skip those cells.

``` python
assert site_hint('https://www.coles.com.au/search/products?q=milk')['cart'].endswith('/trolley')
assert site_hint('https://www.amazon.com.au/s?k=x')['search'] == 'https://www.amazon.com.au/s?k={q}'
assert site_hint('https://members.ceresfairfood.org.au/products/search')['note']
assert site_hint('https://some-random-shopify-store.com') == {}     # generic path, no hints needed
```

``` python
#: A checkout form with Australian terms, mixed autocomplete coverage, and decoy fields.
FORM = [
    dict(i=0, tag='input', type='search', name='q', id='', autocomplete=None, label='Search parts', options=None),
    dict(i=1, tag='input', type='email', name='customer[email]', id='e', autocomplete='email', label='Email address', options=None),
    dict(i=2, tag='input', type='text', name='firstName', id='', autocomplete='off', label='', options=None),
    dict(i=3, tag='input', type='text', name='ship[ln]', id='', autocomplete='family-name', label='Family name', options=None),
    dict(i=4, tag='input', type='tel', name='contact', id='', autocomplete='tel', label='Email or phone', options=None),
    dict(i=5, tag='input', type='text', name='address1', id='', autocomplete=None, label='Address', options=None),
    dict(i=6, tag='input', type='text', name='address2', id='', autocomplete=None, label='Address line 2', options=None),
    dict(i=7, tag='input', type='text', name='locality', id='', autocomplete='address-level2', label='Suburb', options=None),
    dict(i=8, tag='select', type='select-one', name='region', id='', autocomplete='address-level1', label='State / Territory',
         options=[dict(v='VIC', t='Victoria'), dict(v='NSW', t='New South Wales')]),
    dict(i=9, tag='input', type='text', name='zip', id='', autocomplete='postal-code', label='Postcode', options=None),
]
hit = match_fields(FORM, dict(email='a@b.co', first_name='Sam', last_name='Nguyen', phone='0400 000 111',
                              address1='12 Smith St', address2='Unit 3', city='Brunswick',
                              state='Victoria', postcode='3056'))
assert {k: v['i'] for k, v in hit.items()} == {'email': 1, 'first_name': 2, 'last_name': 3, 'phone': 4,
                                              'address1': 5, 'address2': 6, 'city': 7, 'state': 8, 'postcode': 9}
assert hit['city']['label'] == 'Suburb'          # Use the autocomplete token instead of the label.
assert hit['first_name']['name'] == 'firstName'  # Use the name when autocomplete is off.

# The autocomplete token takes priority over a misleading label.
assert _score(FORM[4], 'email') == 0 and _score(FORM[4], 'phone') == 100
assert _score(FORM[0], 'first_name') == 0        # The search box does not match this key.
# Each field is used once. Unmatched keys are reported.
assert len({v['i'] for v in hit.values()}) == len(hit)
assert match_fields(FORM, dict(card_cvc='123')) == {}
```

``` python
#: An explicit variant takes priority over the card variant id. An unmatched variant is rejected.
class _VPage:
    async def eval(self, js): return 'https://x/p' if js == 'location.href' else [dict(id='1', name='Small'), dict(id='2', name='Large')]
_card = dict(url='https://x/p', vid='1')
assert (await _variant_id(_VPage(), _card, 'Large'))[0] == '2'
assert (await _variant_id(_VPage(), _card, 'Huge'))[0] is None
assert (await _variant_id(_VPage(), _card, None))[0] == '1'
assert (await _variant_id(_VPage(), _card, 'L'))[0] is None   # Both names contain 'L', but neither equals it. The code does not guess.
assert (await _variant_id(_VPage(), _card, 'large'))[0] == '2'

class _XLPage:
    async def eval(self, js): return 'https://x/p' if js == 'location.href' else [dict(id='3', name='X-Large'), dict(id='4', name='Large')]
assert (await _variant_id(_XLPage(), _card, 'Large'))[0] == '4'   # An exact name takes priority over a name that contains it.
assert (await _variant_id(_XLPage(), _card, 'X-L'))[0] == '3'

class _NoVariants:
    async def shop_prep(self): return 'shopify'
    async def shop_products(self): return [dict(i=0, title='Tee', url='https://x/p', vid='1', add=True)]
    async def eval(self, js): return 'https://x/p' if js == 'location.href' else []
res = await Page.shop_add(_NoVariants(), 0, 1, 'Large')
assert res['ok'] is False and res['need'] == 'variant' and 'nothing was added' in res['error']
```

``` python
#: Verify that only an exposed cart signal change counts.
assert _changed(dict(count=0, subtotal=0), dict(count=1, subtotal=9.5)) == 'count'
assert _changed(dict(count=None, subtotal=10.0), dict(count=None, subtotal=19.5)) == 'subtotal'
assert _changed(dict(count=1, subtotal=9.5), dict(count=1, subtotal=9.5)) == ''
assert _changed(dict(count=1), dict(count=None)) == ''     # A blank reading is not progress.
assert _changed(dict(count=1, lines=[{'title': 'a', 'qty': 1}]),
                dict(count=1, lines=[{'title': 'a', 'qty': 1}, {'title': 'b', 'qty': 1}])) == 'lines'
```

``` python
#: Product selection does not guess. An invalid request raises an error and lists the available products.
ITEMS = [dict(i=0, title='Oil Filter Z145A', related=None), dict(i=1, title='Oil Filter Z411', related=None),
         dict(i=2, title='Oil Filter Z411 Twin Pack', related=None), dict(i=3, title='Oil Filter Z145A', related=True)]
assert _match(ITEMS, 1)['i'] == 1
assert _match(ITEMS, '1')['i'] == 1                        # A string index.
assert _match(ITEMS, 'Oil Filter Z411')['i'] == 1          # An exact title takes priority over a longer title.
assert _match(ITEMS, 'twin pack')['i'] == 2                # A case-insensitive substring.
assert _match(ITEMS, 'Oil Filter Z145A')['i'] == 0         # The product takes priority over the recommendation.
for bad in ('flux capacitor', 9):
    try:
        _match(ITEMS, bad)
        raise AssertionError(f'{bad!r} should not have matched')
    except ShopError as e: assert 'Z145A' in str(e) or 'page has 4' in str(e), e
```

``` python
#: The payment guard covers common checkout labels.
for label in ('Pay now', 'Place order', 'Complete order', 'Confirm purchase', 'Buy now', 'Submit order'):
    assert PAY_RX.search(label), label
for label in ('Continue to shipping', 'Save address', 'Apply discount', 'Update cart'):
    assert not PAY_RX.search(label), label
```

``` python
#: Line lookup and numeric fill keys report page values without guessing.
CART = dict(count=2, subtotal=13.0, lines=[dict(i=0, text='Apples', qty='2', qty_kind='select', remove=True),
                                           dict(i=1, text='Pears', qty='1', qty_kind=None, remove=True)])
assert _line(CART, 1)['text'] == 'Pears' and _line(CART, '0')['qty_kind'] == 'select'
try:
    _line(CART, 5)
    raise AssertionError('line 5 should not have resolved')
except ShopError as e: assert 'cart page shows 2' in str(e), e

#: A numeric profile key addresses a `fields()` index and does not use `FIELD_MAP`.
assert match_fields(FORM, {'7': 'Large', 'city': 'Brunswick'})['city']['i'] == 7   # '7' is a field index, not a profile key.
assert _origin('https://shop.example.com/collections/all?x=1') == 'https://shop.example.com'
```

### Live stores

These cells run against Allbirds, a Shopify store, and CERES Fair Food,
a custom store. The tests skip these cells.

``` python
s = shop('https://www.allbirds.com')
s.search('tree runner')[:2]
```

``` python
# No size is chosen when several sizes are in stock.
r = s.add(0)
r.get('need'), [v['name'] for v in (r.get('variants') or [])][:3]
```

``` python
s.add(0, qty=2, variant='9')        # The result contains ok=True, how='count', and a variant_id.
```

``` python
s.cart(lines=True), s.set_qty(0, 1), s.remove(0)
```

``` python
# CERES Fair Food uses a custom Rails store with "Add" buttons and quantity selects.
c = shop('https://members.ceresfairfood.org.au')
[(p['title'], p['price'], p['qty']) for p in c.search('apples')[:3]]
```

``` python
# When logged out, no cart signal exists. The result reports this state.
c.add('Apples Fuji Organic 500g', qty=2)   # The result contains ok=None, an error, and blockers.
```

## Limits

fossick does not solve captchas. It never clicks a payment button unless
the call passes `confirm=True`. Store pages change over time. The
in-page script can stop finding a store’s controls. Every action checks
the cart and reports what it found. It does not assume that a click
worked.
